competitors.title: The 2026-07-28 MCP Specification Release Candidate
key_points: MCP becomes stateless at the protocol layer — removes initialize/initialized handshake and Mcp-Session-Id header
Every request carries protocol version, client identity, and capabilities in _meta
New server/discover RPC for capability advertisement and version negotiation
Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR) pattern replaces server-initiated requests via InputRequiredResult
Streamable HTTP now requires Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers for routing without body inspection
List results carry ttlMs and cacheScope for client-side caching
W3C Trace Context propagation documented for OpenTelemetry compatibility
Extensions become first-class with reverse-DNS IDs and independent versioning
MCP Apps extension for server-rendered interactive UIs in sandboxed iframes
Tasks graduates from experimental core feature to official extension with redesigned lifecycle
Roots, Sampling, and Logging features deprecated with 12-month minimum window
Full JSON Schema 2020-12 support for tool inputSchema and outputSchema
Release candidate locked May 21, 2026; final specification ships July 28, 2026

competitors.title: MCP Specification Key Changes (Draft Changelog)
key_points: Protocol-level sessions and Mcp-Session-Id header removed from Streamable HTTP
Initialize/initialized handshake removed — version, identity, capabilities travel in _meta per request
New server/discover method for up-front capability probing
HTTP GET endpoint and resources/subscribe replaced with subscriptions/listen single stream
Ping, logging/setLevel, and roots/list_changed notifications removed
Log level set per-request via io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel in _meta
Experimental tasks moved to io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension with polling via tasks/get
MRTR pattern replaces server-initiated requests with InputRequiredResult + retry
All results now carry required resultType field (complete or input_required)
SSE stream resumability and Last-Event-ID removed — broken streams require re-issuing requests
Resource not found error code changed from -32002 to -32602 (JSON-RPC standard)
Error codes renumbered: HeaderMismatch -32001→-32020, MissingRequiredClientCapability -32003→-32021, UnsupportedProtocolVersion -32004→-32022
OAuth iss parameter validation required per RFC 9207
Dynamic Client Registration deprecated in favor of Client ID Metadata Documents

competitors.title: MCP Deprecated Features Registry
key_points: Roots deprecated in 2026-07-28 — migrate to tool parameters, resource URIs, or server configuration
Sampling deprecated in 2026-07-28 — integrate directly with LLM provider APIs
Logging deprecated in 2026-07-28 — use stderr for stdio or OpenTelemetry for observability
HTTP+SSE transport deprecated since 2025-03-26 — migrate to Streamable HTTP
includeContext values thisServer/allServers deprecated — omit field or use none
Dynamic Client Registration deprecated in 2026-07-28 — use Client ID Metadata Documents
Earliest removal for all 2026-07-28 deprecations: first revision on or after 2027-07-28
No features have been removed yet under the new lifecycle policy

competitors.title: MCP Feature Lifecycle and Deprecation Policy
key_points: Three feature states: Active, Deprecated, Removed
Minimum 12-month deprecation window between Deprecated and earliest possible removal
Deprecation requires a SEP with rationale, migration path, and minimum window specification
Deprecated features gain @deprecated JSDoc tags, prose notices, changelog entries, and registry entries
Tier 1 SDKs must mark deprecated API surface and emit runtime warnings
Expedited removal possible for active security risks with 90-day minimum
Deprecated features can be restored to Active by superseding SEP
Removed features remain documented in the Final revision they last appeared in

stats.fact: MCP 2026-07-28 is the largest revision of the protocol since launch, delivering on the 2026 roadmap
A remote MCP server that previously needed sticky sessions, a shared session store, and deep packet inspection can now run behind a plain round-robin load balancer
The release candidate was locked on May 21, 2026; final specification ships July 28, 2026
Six SEPs work together to make MCP stateless at the protocol layer: SEP-2575, SEP-2567, SEP-2260, SEP-2322, SEP-2243, SEP-2549
Roots, Sampling, and Logging are deprecated with earliest removal on or after 2027-07-28
The HTTP+SSE transport has been deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26
Error codes renumbered: HeaderMismatch -32001→-32020, MissingRequiredClientCapability -32003→-32021, UnsupportedProtocolVersion -32004→-32022
Resource not found error code changed from MCP-custom -32002 to JSON-RPC standard -32602 (Invalid Params)
The MCP specification repository has 8,500+ GitHub stars and 4,285+ commits as of June 2026
MCP was created by David Soria Parra and Justin Spahr-Summers at Anthropic
The feature lifecycle policy mandates a minimum 12-month deprecation window, with 90-day minimum for expedited security-related removals
